edges.description: Without functional BAF activity at typical enhancers, lineage differentiation programmes are never activated and PRC2-mediated repression goes unopposed.
Progenitors held in an undifferentiated, proliferative state give rise to malignant rhabdoid tumours.
Smarcb1 loss in early neural crest generates cranial nerve and meningeal tumours with the histology and molecular profile of human rhabdoid tumours.
edges.limitations: The tumours arise in cranial nerves and meninges rather than the infratentorial sites typical of human ATRT, and the model uses conditional somatic deletion rather than a constitutional heterozygous allele with a stochastic second hit.

nodes.description: Carriers are followed with whole-body MRI from diagnosis and an age-stratified schedule of clinical examination, abdominal and neck ultrasound, and brain and spine MRI, intensive in the first years of life and relaxing after age five.

evidence.snippet: Age 19 months to five years. Every three months, thorough clinical examination including neurologic examination, ultrasound of the abdomen and neck, and brain and spine MRI.

nodes.description: A conditional knockout series that varies the developmental timing of Smarcb1 loss, showing that the same gene produces rhabdoid tumours or schwannomas depending on when in development the allele is lost.
nodes.id: Conditional Smarcb1 and Nf2 knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: Timing of Smarcb1 and Nf2 inactivation determines schwannoma versus rhabdoid tumor development.
evidence.snippet: Germline mutations of the SMARCB1 gene predispose to two distinct tumor syndromes: rhabdoid tumor predisposition syndrome, with malignant pediatric tumors mostly developing in brain and kidney, and familial schwannomatosis, with adulthood benign tumors involving cranial and peripheral nerves.

nodes.description: Without functional BAF activity at typical enhancers, lineage differentiation programmes are not activated and progenitors remain in a proliferative, undifferentiated state. Loss of BAF-mediated opposition to PRC2 leaves EZH2-dependent repression unchecked at these loci.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanisms by which SMARCB1 loss drives rhabdoid tumor growth.
evidence.snippet: deletion of SMARCB1 led to elevated expression and recruitment of EZH2 to Polycomb targets that became broadly H3K27-trimethylated and repressed in SMARCB1-deficient fibroblasts and cancers

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline deletion, nonsense or frameshift SMARCB1 allele provides the constitutional first hit in every cell of the developing child.

evidence.reference_title: Spectrum of SMARCB1/INI1 mutations in familial and sporadic rhabdoid tumors.
evidence.snippet: Germline mutations and deletions of SMARCB1/INI1 in chromosome band 22q11.2 predispose patients to rhabdoid tumor and schwannomatosis.

evidence.reference_title: Spectrum of SMARCB1/INI1 mutations in familial and sporadic rhabdoid tumors.
evidence.snippet: Approximately one-third of newly diagnosed patients with rhabdoid tumor have an underlying genetic predisposition to tumors due to a germline SMARCB1 alteration.

nodes.description: The arrested progenitor gives rise to a malignant rhabdoid tumour, which may arise in the central nervous system as atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumour, in the kidney, or in extrarenal soft tissue, and in RTPS1 frequently at more than one site synchronously.

animal_models.description: Smarcb1 loss in early neural crest generates cranial nerve and meningeal tumours with the histology and molecular profile of human rhabdoid tumours.
animal_models.genotype: Tissue- and developmental-stage-specific conditional Smarcb1 and/or Nf2 deletion

evidence.reference_title: Spectrum of SMARCB1/INI1 mutations in familial and sporadic rhabdoid tumors.
evidence.snippet: These abnormalities included point and frameshift mutations, intragenic deletions and duplications, and larger deletions including regions both proximal and distal to SMARCB1.

evidence.reference_title: Constitutional balanced translocations involving SMARCB1: A rare cause of rhabdoid tumor predisposition syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Most known RTPS1-related SMARCB1 gene mutations are copy number variants (CNVs) or single nucleotide variants/indels, but structural variant analysis (SVA) is not usually included in the molecular evaluation.

evidence.reference_title: SMARCB1 mutations in schwannomatosis and genotype correlations with rhabdoid tumors.
evidence.snippet: Comparison with germline SMARCB1 mutations in patients with rhabdoid tumors showed that the schwannomatosis mutations were significantly more likely to occur at either end of the gene and be nontruncating mutations (P < 0.0001).

nodes.description: Loss of the SMARCB1 core subunit does not dismantle the BAF complex, which still assembles without it. What it destabilises is the complex's chromatin occupancy: targeting to promoters and typical enhancers is impaired and the complex is redistributed away from the sites it normally maintains. The distinction matters, because it makes rhabdoid tumorigenesis an epigenetic mislocalisation defect rather than a loss of remodelling capacity.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanisms by which SMARCB1 loss drives rhabdoid tumor growth.
evidence.snippet: SMARCB1 (INI1/SNF5/BAF47), a core subunit of the SWI/SNF (BAF) chromatin-remodeling complex, is inactivated in the large majority of rhabdoid tumors, and germline heterozygous SMARCB1 mutations form the basis for rhabdoid predisposition syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanisms by which SMARCB1 loss drives rhabdoid tumor growth.
evidence.snippet: It has been reported dispensable for formation of the SWI/SNF complex (42) but implicated in contributing to the targeting of the SWI/SNF complex to promoters (43).

evidence.reference_title: Mechanisms by which SMARCB1 loss drives rhabdoid tumor growth.
evidence.snippet: Given the absence of genomic instability despite the rapidity by which SMARCB1 deficient cancers arise both in humans and mice, these findings collectively suggest that the initiation and progression of aggressive cancers caused by SMARCB1 loss may not arise due to effects upon genome integrity, but rather epigenetically via perturbation of transcriptional regulation.

nodes.description: Loss of the remaining wild-type allele in a susceptible progenitor, typically by deletion or copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity, completes biallelic inactivation and initiates the tumour.
nodes.id: Somatic Inactivation of the Second SMARCB1 Allele

evidence.reference_title: Mechanisms by which SMARCB1 loss drives rhabdoid tumor growth.
evidence.snippet: Mouse models validated Smarcb1 as a bona fide tumor suppressor, as Smarcb1 inactivation in mice results in 100% of the animals rapidly developing cancer.
